guideBlocks.title: Requirements
items: PS4 with GoldHEN enabled and plugin support.
Call of Duty: Black Ops 4, CUSA12446, updated to 1.26. The supplied README states that other versions cause the plugin to shut down.

items.title: Transfer the plugin
items.text: Using the GoldHEN FTP server on port 2121, copy b33_bo4.prx to /data/GoldHEN/plugins/b33_bo4.prx.

items.title: Add its game entry
items.text: In /data/GoldHEN/plugins.ini, add the configuration below. If [CUSA12446] already exists, add the plugin path beneath that section.

items.title: Launch Black Ops 4
items.text: After a few seconds, the plugin displays: B33 EXP - L1 + R3 to open.

guideBlocks.title: plugins.ini entry
guideBlocks.text:
[CUSA12446]
/data/GoldHEN/plugins/b33_bo4.prx

guideBlocks.title: Usage
guideBlocks.text: Wait a few seconds at the main menu before starting a game. The plugin loads the B33 script automatically; no external injector is required. In a LAN Multiplayer or Zombies match with bots, use L1 + R3 to open or close the menu. The menu switches between Multiplayer and Zombies modes automatically.

guideBlocks.title: Status and co-host menu
items: LIVE in the top-right corner means the script is active.
NO GSC means the script failed to load; restart the game.
Players → player name → Co-Host Menu enables the other player’s menu. That player opens it with L2 + knife.

guideBlocks.title: Uninstall
guideBlocks.text: Remove the plugin line from plugins.ini, or delete b33_bo4.prx.

resources.name: BO2 Relay setup guide
resources.description: PC-host instructions for the BO2 Resurge and Microsoft Store clients, as described by the supplied tutorial.

images.caption: Relay screenshot supplied with the forum post.

guideBlocks.title: Scope of the supplied tutorial
guideBlocks.text: This is a Windows PC-host setup for the BO2 Resurge or Microsoft Store client. The source describes a UDP relay for friends joining a custom game behind NAT. It does not establish PS4/PS5 game compatibility. The associated packages are not offered here while their distribution/capture review remains incomplete.

guideBlocks.title: Prepare the host
items: Install Wireshark with Npcap selected, then install WinPcap 4.1.3. The source calls for both capture drivers, in that order. Reboot after both installations.
Confirm that Wireshark lists the active Ethernet or Wi-Fi interface. The source runs RUN_GUI.exe with administrator privileges.
Keep the relay package, supported PC game client and access to the router configuration available.

items.title: Record the host and gateway addresses
items.text: Run ipconfig in Command Prompt. Under the active adapter, note IPv4 Address for the host PC and Default Gateway for the router. The tutorial recommends a DHCP reservation or static host address.

items.title: Set the router forwarding rule
items.text: Open the default gateway address and find Port Forwarding/NAT. Forward external UDP 3074 to internal UDP 3077 at the host PC’s IPv4 address. Enable and save the rule.

guideBlocks.title: Source port mapping
guideBlocks.text:
Protocol: UDP
External game port: 3074
Internal relay port: 3077
Destination: host PC IPv4 address

guideBlocks.title: Open the custom game before starting the relay

items.title: Prepare RUN_GUI
items.text: Open the relay tool as administrator. Set Game Port to 3074 and Relay Port to 3077. Do not choose Start yet.

items.title: Open the lobby
items.text: Launch the supported PC client and open a Custom Game lobby/map first.

items.title: Start the relay
items.text: Return to RUN_GUI and choose Start. Check the traffic/log output, then have a friend test joining through the public address or the client’s normal invite method.

guideBlocks.title: VPS option in the tutorial
items: The source offers a VPS with public IPv4 when home forwarding is unavailable, including CGNAT/shared-network setups.
It opens inbound UDP 3074 and 3077 in both provider and operating-system firewalls, with outbound UDP permitted.
Its alternatives are the same relay on the VPS pointed at the home/public or VPN address, or WireGuard forwarding VPS UDP 3074 to the home client’s UDP 3077. Friends join the VPS public address.
The Windows machine running RUN_GUI still needs the packet-capture drivers.

guideBlocks.title: Check a failed connection
items: For missing traffic, check both capture drivers, required permissions, the selected active network interface and the custom-game-before-Start order.
For join failures, check UDP forwarding, the host address, double NAT and CGNAT. Use a UDP-specific test rather than a TCP-only port checker.
If the setup stops working after a reboot, confirm that the host PC address has not changed. Preserve the full error text and relay logs when reporting a problem.

guideBlocks.title: Screenshot and written ports
guideBlocks.text: The supplied screenshot shows Relay 3076 and Game 3074 as interface defaults. The attached written tutorial uses Relay 3077 and Game 3074. These source differences do not establish console compatibility.

guideBlocks.title: MWR-specific setup from the supplied guide

items.title: Extract the full package
items.text: Keep the Tools folder and other supplied files together. In the launcher, choose the Modern Warfare Remastered tool.

items.title: Prepare the PS4 game
items.text: Enable GoldHEN and its bin loader, launch Modern Warfare Remastered update 1.15 and open Multiplayer.

items.title: Send debug and connect
items.text: On the tool Home page, enter the PS4 IP address and use Send ps4debug (Envoyer ps4debug), port 9090. Wait for the console notification, then choose Connect (Connecter).

items.title: Use the built-in menu
items.text: On the GSC Injector page, leave the .gscbin field empty to select the built-in MAG menu.

items.title: Enable automatic injection
items.text: Stay at the Multiplayer main menu, enable Auto inject (Injection auto), and keep the tool open and connected. The guide explains that MWR restarts its Multiplayer process between menus and matches, so automatic injection restores the menu.

items.title: Host a private match
items.text: Start a private match as host; the menu loads with the map. Remove (Retirer) at the Multiplayer menu or restart the game to unload it.

guideBlocks.title: AI Zombies mode
guideBlocks.text: In the menu, use GameMode → AI Zombies and choose a map. The source recommends a private team match, such as Team Deathmatch. The match restarts followed by two ten-second countdowns; selecting an AI Zombies entry again stops the mode.

guideBlocks.title: AI Zombies map choices in the guide
items: Backlot, Ambush, Bloc, Vacant, Overgrown, Crash, Bog, Countdown, Crossfire, District, Downpour, Pipeline, Shipment, Showdown, Strike and Wet Work.

guideBlocks.title: Custom GSC scripts
items: The Compilation card accepts a .gsc file or a folder of .gsc files, then compiles a .gscbin.
Define init(); the guide says it is called for matches and the menu lobby. Its menu-lobby map name is mp_vlobby_room, where the script should return immediately.
Supported includes are maps\mp\_utility, maps\mp\gametypes\_hud_util and common_scripts\utility in compiler\include.
The stated limit is 128 KB of bytecode per script. Fully restart MWR if the tool reports that the injection area is full.
The source identifies gsc-tool as the compiler, licensed GPL-3.0; its license file is included in the archive.

guideBlocks.title: Diagnostics and credits
guideBlocks.text: The Journal card and MAG_GSC_INJECTOR_MWR.log beside the executable record each step. Developers credited by the MWR guide: UrBaaZz and Zerty.

guideBlocks.title: Separate upstream release
guideBlocks.text: This entry comes from the publisher’s tagged v2.2.0 release, reached through the HYDRA project linked in the captured forum post. It does not replace the unavailable v1.0.0 forum build. The project also lists newer releases; the file offered here is explicitly v2.2.0.

items: WWII: a PS4 GSC injector and Hydra menus for Multiplayer and Zombies.

guideBlocks.title: Compatibility details

guideBlocks.title: Saved Windows package
guideBlocks.text: Only the Windows portable ZIP from this release was added. Its 90,946,143 bytes match the SHA-256 digest published by GitHub. A local archive copy is retained; the download button links the exact publisher asset. The package has not been executed.
